---
title: "Research"
subtitle: "Computational methods for heritage, structures and materials"
---

My research connects numerical methods in structural mechanics with the study of
existing buildings and construction materials. The work ranges from survey data
and automatic model generation to finite-element formulations, coupled
degradation models and experimental characterisation.

## Modelling cultural heritage from survey to structure {#cultural-heritage-modelling}

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-5}
![Cloud2FEM transforms a point-cloud survey into a finite-element mesh.](assets/img/research-lines/cultural-heritage-cloud2fem.png){.research-line-cover}
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-7}
Point clouds, photogrammetry and BIM provide different views of an existing
structure. I develop workflows that turn these records into analysis-ready
models, then use those models to investigate structural behaviour, damage and
conservation questions. Applications include towers, walls, vaults, bridges
and complex historic buildings.

**Selected work:** [Cloud2FEM: a finite-element mesh generator based on point
clouds (2022)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.softx.2022.101099); [numerical
modelling-based damage diagnostics (2023)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.culher.2023.02.004);
[FE and BIM modelling from point-cloud transformation (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1080/15583058.2024.2330942).

## Digital twinning and structural ontologies {#digital-twinning-and-structural-ontologies}

Structural digital twins bring together finite-element models, monitoring
measurements, survey data and asset records. Ontologies and semantic data models
can make the meaning and provenance of these different sources explicit, so that
data remain connected and traceable as a structure is surveyed, modelled,
analysed and monitored. This line develops methods and software for organising
that information and linking it to structural models, with a focus on digital
twins of existing and historic buildings.

**Selected work:** [Integrating BIM and cloud-based solutions for cultural
heritage management (2023)](https://doi.org/10.3390/heritage6120384);
[FE and BIM modelling from point-cloud transformation (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1080/15583058.2024.2330942).

## Adaptive and reliable finite-element procedures {#finite-element-procedures}

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-5}
![Adaptive mesh refinement guided by recovery-based error estimation.](assets/img/research-lines/adaptive-procedures-rcp.png){.research-line-cover}
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-7}
This line concerns the procedures that make finite-element analyses accurate
and practical: recovery by compatibility in patches (RCP), a-posteriori error
estimation, adaptive refinement and automated assessment workflows. The aim is
to direct computation to the regions that govern the response and to make
complex analyses more repeatable.

**Selected work:** [Adaptivity based on recovery by compatibility in patches
(2010)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.finel.2009.12.004); [an automated two-step
procedure based on adaptive limit and pushover analyses (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compstruc.2021.106561);
[force-displacement descriptions of masonry collapse mechanisms (2020)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compstruc.2020.106234).
:::
:::

## Finite-element formulations for plates, shells and beams {#finite-element-formulations}

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-5}
![Displacement and strain fields from the Q4RS shell benchmark.](assets/img/research-lines/finite-elements-q4rs.png){.research-line-cover}
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-7}
I develop finite elements that remain accurate and stable under bending,
transverse shear, material nonlinearity and mesh distortion. This includes the
nodally integrated plate element (NIPE), patch-averaged assumed-strain elements
(PASE), the Q4RS Reissner–Mindlin shell, and beam elements with semi-rigid
connections.

**Selected work:** [The NIPE-based nine-node plate element (2012)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.finel.2012.04.004);
[PASE elements for stress analysis (2012)](https://doi.org/10.1002/nme.4264);
[the Q4RS shell element (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.finel.2026.104574);
[shear-deformable beams with semi-rigid connections (2012)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jcsr.2012.07.024).

[FEM shell benchmarks](gallery/2026-02-fem-shell.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary .btn-sm}
:::
:::

## Multiphysics of salt transport and material degradation {#multiphysics}

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-5}
![Coupled saturation, tortuosity, stress and damage fields in a salt-crystallisation model.](assets/img/research-lines/multiphysics-salt-damage.png){.research-line-cover}
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-7}
Salt weathering links moisture and heat transport, ion movement,
crystallisation and mechanical damage. I study coupled and staggered
multiphysics models that connect these processes across scales, from porous
materials to masonry walls and retaining structures, to understand how
environmental exposure changes material properties and structural response.

**Selected work:** [A coupled multiphase model for hygrothermal analysis and
salt-crystallisation stress (2013)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2012.12.045);
[a staggered multiphysics framework for salt-induced damage (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2021.124486);
[multiphase modelling of salt weathering in masonry retaining walls (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jobe.2025.112999).
:::
:::

## Sustainable and innovative construction materials {#innovative-materials}

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-5}
![Fabric-reinforced cementitious matrix specimens used in tensile testing.](assets/img/research-lines/sustainable-materials-frcm.png){.research-line-cover}
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-7}
This line combines experimental characterisation with numerical modelling to
evaluate lower-impact materials for construction, strengthening and compatible
repair. Recent work studies sand-free mortars using olive-kernel aggregate and
fabric-reinforced cementitious matrix (FRCM) composites. Collaborative work
with Luis Mercedes studies the contributions of the fabric and cementitious
matrix to tensile behaviour.

**Selected work:** [Sand-free olive-kernel aggregate mortars (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jobe.2026.115755);
[matrix and fabric contributions in FRCM composites (2023)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2022.129693);
[environmental ageing of masonry strengthened with composites (2019)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.engstruct.2019.109773).

[Innovative materials album](gallery/2026-04-innovative-materials.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary .btn-sm}
:::
